messages:
Noah (AE): MercuryTrust reached out. They want to swap VendorX for Redwood. Key asks: 1) tiny compatibility shim, 2) behavioral parity on 250 golden prompts, 3) billing delta analysis, 4) completed security questionnaire, 5) rollback runbook for canary. Who can lead SE and Eng?

Riley (Sales Eng): I'll run SE. Proposed quick plan: collect 250 prompts + 48h sample traffic, build a 1-file proxy, run parity harness, estimate cost delta, and do a 48h canary in eu-central.

Emma (MercuryTrust Eng): To add: VendorX uses header X-Vendor-Session + nested body.convos. Our UI relies on streamed partials (flush on sentence). Will streaming differences break UX?

Samir (Runtime Eng): Streaming behavior may differ. Redwood streams by token boundaries; VendorX may flush on sentence punctuation. We can add a small client-side debounce or reconcile on the shim to preserve UX. Also function-calling: VendorX always returns a single `action` object; Redwood can return multiple candidates if requested. We'll default to top-1 for parity.

Riley (Sales Eng): Quick pseudo-shim to propose for their infra team:
```
// shim: vendorx -> redwood
let msgs = body.convos.flatMap(c=>c.messages).map(m=>({role:m.role,content:m.text}));
fetch('https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate',{method:'POST',body:JSON.stringify({model:'rwd-1',messages:msgs})});
```
This keeps adapter <200 lines and avoids deep integration.

Emma (MercuryTrust Eng): Good. Billing: VendorX bills by "chunks" rounded up; we saw overcharging on long prompts. Need a realistic cost model for our 8k-char average prompts and ~4 exchanges per session.

Samir (Runtime Eng): Ask them to drop a 72h dump. We'll tokenize their payload, run our hosted vs reserved pricing, and return a delta. We'll include quantization/compact model options to show cost/latency tradeoffs.

Jin (Security): Send the questionnaire link here and ask legal to fill. Main checks: SOC2 Type II, SSO + SCIM, CMK support, VPC peering options, EU-only data residency confirmation, and pen-test report. Also need to know log retention and redact options.

Noah (AE): Jin, link please.

Jin (Security): Questionnaire: https://redwood.internal/sec/questionnaire-v3. Also note: if they require customer-managed HSM, that pushes into Private deployment.

ops-bot: staging-mercury-9 spun up in eu-central-1

Riley (Sales Eng): Parity eval approach: 1) exact string checks for templated flows, 2) semantic similarity (embedding cosine >= 0.86), 3) function contract compliance (schema + invocation count). We will return a CSV with pass/fail and sample diffs.

Emma (MercuryTrust Eng): Acceptance criteria: critical alerts must be <=2% divergence, non-critical <=10%. I'll confirm with product.

Samir (Runtime Eng): For canary rollback runbook: shim supports header X-Canary=true to route to canary cluster; mirror traffic and allow failover to VendorX via routing flag. We'll produce a one-page runbook.

Noah (AE): Commercials: can we offer a migration credit? They are evaluating Dedicated for 12 months likely.

Riley (Sales Eng): We can propose up to $12k engineering credit for 12-month commit or cover up to 60 hours. I'll include that in the handoff.

Jin (Security): Request: MercuryTrust to provide VendorX retention policy + any third-party audit they have. That speeds legal review.

Emma (MercuryTrust Eng): I'll get the 72h dump and the 250 golden prompts by EOD tomorrow. Also legal will start the questionnaire.

Riley (Sales Eng): Eng availability: Samir can allocate 0.6 FTE week 1, 0.2 FTE for canary. Samir, confirm?

Samir (Runtime Eng): Confirmed. I'll also prepare the token-count script and the parity harness.

Noah (AE): Great. I'll schedule kickoff for Tuesday 09:00 CET and attach the sec questionnaire + migration credit term sheet. Thanks everyone :rocket:
